items.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: So I asked, I said, “you know I was at your home.”

ctx.x: Aw, gee. You think Lester just kind of ran out of gas?

He had his problems. He drank a lot, he used marijuana a lot, probably heroin as well. And he died not too long after that show. It’s interesting though, I did get to see him and interview him maybe three or four years before then in his home in Queens, one of the times he was off the road. And he was very lucid then, and we had a long talk. And he was telling me, he says, you know I never play a ballad unless I learn the lyrics first, because I want to get the sense of what they had in mind when they wrote it.…

because you were coming and he wanted quiet.” But then he told me he said every time Lester came off the road that one of the first things he did was to go to the school to find out how the kid was doing. So much for the jazz men who don’t care about anything but the ambience of the music.
